doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Pepsi campaign lines and the writing competition
summary: Phillips tells how BBDO and Pepsi had writers compete for lines like Pepsi the generous one and Pepsi pours it on.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Yes it sure did. Many deadlines loomed. But the funniest one really, Pepsi Cola, now they had [sings] come alive, you’re in Pepsi generation. Joanie Sommers singing a nice swinging tune. But it was the early ‘60s and the people that were getting married and having kids really didn’t grow up on that music. They grew up on the early Welk stuff. And so I spoke to several music houses about doing it. I wasn’t singing a lot of jingles. I didn’t really have that jingly sound as a soloist. But I did talk to them about doing some, you know, more rock. And they said well maybe for a couple of chain products but not across the board. And so I happened to meet Scott Muny’s brother, anyway introduced us to Hillary Lipsitz who was at BBDO. And Hillary believed that we should be, that their commercials should be more rock-influenced. And so I took “Come Alive” and I did it first with studio people and then did it with the Hondells, the Four Tops, Martha and the Vandellas, and Del Shannon. Anyway they just went on, they were for the youth market on radio. And then came the new campaign. Now when a new campaign is born it’s the lyric and what they’re selling, how they’re going to sell Pepsi. Right? Well the first line that came up, and this time they were not as later came, that they were giving it out to the world and anybody off the street could write it. But this was just given to the four of us: Sid Raymond — I think there were four of us who had done Pepsi commercials. And so we each had to write. Now the very first, and I’ll embarrass anybody from BBDO, was
“Pepsi the generous one” which got to be known around the halls of BBDO as “Peppy the generous swan.”
Oh that’s so interesting, yes, because you can’t sing that very well.

I wrote it, and we did a demo on it, and the client didn’t like it. Well I hope not. So then they came up with “the taste that beats the others cold.” Okay. So we all had to write the taste that beats the others cold. Thank God I won that competition again. And then “Pepsi pours it on” was the next line they came up with. So we all wrote that, did a whole demo on it and so forth, and they couldn’t agree. And so between the client and advertising agency, they said, “Well let’s put them together and do the whole thing. Write “taste that beats the others cold/Pepsi pours it on.” And so I did, and thank God I won that competition too. And that’s how I happened to do it with the Four Tops again and —
